Introduction

[edit | edit source]

Hello! Welcome to the Ultimate Ironman Walkthrough Guide to Prifddinas. This guide provides a complete step-by-step walkthrough for Ultimate Ironmen to complete the Song of the Elves quest and many other foundations, starting all the way from account creation. Completing this quest allows access to the city of Prifddinas which has many extremely useful features such as The Gauntlet, carnivorous chinchompas, a sawmill, shops, Zalcano, soft clay rocks, a house portal with respawn location nearby, and more. These benefits, along with the high skill requirements of the quest, make completion of Song of the Elves a significant milestone for any Ultimate Ironman account and will leave the player with a solid foundation moving forward.

Ultimate Ironman Discord

Guide:Ultimate Ironman Walkthrough Guide/PvM Route (This is a gear routing guide for direction after you complete Song of the Elves).

Guide Structure and Target Audience.

[edit | edit source]

When embarking on your journey with this guide it can be helpful to understand some of the design philosophy and limitations that influence its design.

In short, this guide is targeted at the average player with OSRS experience on another account but who is new to the Ultimate Ironman mode.

If you are interested in a more detailed breakdown of how the guide is structured, expand the section below.

I have it hidden because this is just optional reading and I don't want to overwhelm people with a wall of text.

Breakdown of Route Design and Philosophy
  • Maintenance: Something important to be aware of is that this guide is actively maintained and updated as I receive feedback and the game is updated. This means that the guide might unexpectedly change while you are in the middle of your journey. Additionally, practically speaking, I cannot personally test every change I make. I have to just mentally think through it and try to write it as best I can. However this inevitably leads to me making mistakes. I rely heavily on feedback from those going through the guide to let me know if there are issues or oversights that need to be fixed, so if you see something strange or wrong please let me know! I do sometimes add "Author Notes" for steps that I have added or modified, but have not been able to test myself. If you see one of these and go through that section, I would appreciate your feedback on how it went!
  • Method Intensity: Given that this guide is aimed at the average player, not a max-efficiency gamer, the guide avoids any high-intensity methods such as Tick manipulation or extensive multi-skilling. Instead, it uses a mix of normal low-medium effort methods. You are of course more than welcome to swap in the higher-intensity methods whenever you would like if that is your preference!
  • Multi-Questing: Unlike many other similar guides, this guide does not make heavy use of multi-questing. This is when you partially complete many different quests at once to save a bit of time. Avoiding multi-questing makes the guide vastly easier to understand and follow, easier to maintain, easier to jump into part-way through, easier to deviate from, and overall much more simple. Doing entire quests at once is how normal players play the game, and practically speaking, once you have teleports unlocked it doesn't actually save that much time anyway. If you are trying to be more efficient, then swapping in higher-intensity skilling methods would be vastly more impactful.
  • Alt Methods: Given that the guide assumes you have experience on another account, it does sometimes call out optional ways to use your alt to aid you. However, the guide does not ever require an alt in any way. This is a new change (it used to never mention alting methods), so please let me know about cool alt method ideas!
  • Quests and Inventory Management: Outside of the first early-game section, the guide takes a relatively hands-off approach to completing quests and managing items. You are routinely asked to just complete a quest, and it is up to you to figure out how to collect the items and overcome any specific challenges that quest presents. The assumption is that as an experienced player you will be familiar with how to use resources such as quest helper or the wiki to collect items and complete quests. Additionally, you do have access to the list of upcoming quests so if you would like, you can look ahead and plan out what items you are going to need. The guide generally won't do this for you though as it would add a lot of complexity for relatively small amounts of time saved.
  • Videos: At many points throughout the guide I have included short videos in which I talk about specific topics that would otherwise take too much text to write out or benefit from a visual example. You are encouraged to listen to these videos as you go!

Route Sections

[edit | edit source]
Setting up for Agility

Setting up for Agility

[edit | edit source]
  • (OPTIONAL) If you want to listen to me ramble about the route for an hour listen to this video.
  • Sell all of your starting items to the general store except your Bread and Shrimps.
  • Speak to Count Check and have him teleport you to the Stronghold of security.
  • Pick up some Cooked meat in the longhouse to the north.
    • Hop worlds for more. 6 should be plenty but you could get more if you are scared.
  • Complete the first 3 levels of the Stronghold of security to get your free 10k gp.
  • Home teleport.
  • Buy a bronze axe and a steel axe from Bob.
  • Drop any extra food.
  • Buy a Spade and an empty jug from the general store.
  • Complete X Marks the Spot.
    • Fill the jug with water in the kitchen when you pass by.
    • Do not use the lamp, destroy it to be reclaimed later.
  • Get level 20 Agility at the Draynor Village Rooftop Course.
  • Purchase a Chronicle and 20 Teleport cards.
  • Walk to Ardougne and complete Hazeel Cult.
    • Take the boat in Rimmington to get there.
    • Make sure to side with Hazeel.
  • Complete Monk's Friend.
    • Chop some logs nearby.
    • Make sure to pop some balloons so you don't curse your accounts RNG.
  • Head to the general store in Port Khazard and purchase some Swamp paste and a tinderbox.
  • Chop and burn logs in the area until you reach 30 Firemaking.
  • Complete Sea slug.
  • Drop all of your items except your coins.
  • Get 25 Thieving at cake stalls.
    • Complete Tribal Totem when you can.
  • Get an inventory of cakes, then head over to the Brimhaven Agility Arena.
  • Train there until level 50 Agility.
    • Start by jumping over the Floor spikes (Brimhaven Agility Arena) until you can start collecting tickets consistently. You will need 30 agility to do most, and 40 agility to do all the obstacles.
    • You will finish out 52 Agility while getting money at the Agility Pyramid.
  • Chronicle teleport to Varrock.
  • Complete Shield of Arrav.
    • Join the Phoenix Gang.
      • Buy a shortbow and some iron arrows from the Archery shop to kill Jonny the Beard to save melee xp.
    • If you have an alt, you can join the Black Arm gang and have them kill the Weaponsmaster for you.
      • This saves a lot of combat xp and is easy to do, so strongly consider it.
  • Complete Children of the Sun.
  • Head to Varlamore and complete Ethically Acquired Antiquities until you are in Port Sarim.
    • Use the Charter ship to get to Port Sarim.
  • Buy a Feather from Gerrant
  • Head over to Kourend and complete Client of Kourend. Veos might return your lamp from X marks the spot, destroy it again.
    • During this quest, steal from Fruit stalls until level 31 Thieving.
      • Save any Strange fruit you get for some free run restoration.
    • Use the Client of Kourend lamps on Hitpoints. DO NOT USE THE X MARKS THE SPOT LAMP.
    • During the quest, quickly change to the Arceuus spellbook and back so that you can make house portals with the teleports later.
  • Continue and complete Ethically Acquired Antiquities.
  • Head over to Aldarin in Varlamore.
  • Complete Death on the Isle.
    • Do not fight back during the first fight. It will be completed when you are almost dead.
    • Attacking with the Prop sword does not give xp.
  • Minigame teleport to Clan wars.
  • Store any gp you have in the coffer there.
  • Completely empty your inventory after that.
  • Get 40 Prayer by picking up big bones at the Boneyard and using them on the Chaos Altar.
    • Don't go for Protection from melee at this time.
    • Do not kill anything for a Looting bag. You don't want to level up.
  • Get an iron dagger(p) and a Lockpick from pickpocketing Rogues in the deep wilderness.
    • Get some cakes from Ardougne to use as food. Use the wilderness lever from Ardougne to complete the diary step.
    • When you are poisoning things in the next sections, be careful not to waste combat xp you don't need to. You should have enough on average, but if you waste xp then bad luck could force you to gain an extra level.
      • Seriously, I have had numerous people tell me they had to gain an extra level because they were careless with their xp.
    • Use the Poison plugin on Runelite to help track your attacks and timer.
  • (Optional) If you have an alternate account, you can use a venom alt to help out killing things and conserving combat xp.
    • Watch this video for a quick tutorial on how to do this.
    • Using Wind strike is often a good way to get the needed damage on your UIM in the short time window.
  • Get you cash stack back out of the coffers at Clan Wars. Don't use your minigame teleport to get there.
  • Steal from Aldarin chests until level 50 Thieving.
    • Fishing Trawler minigame teleport, then take the charter ship to Aldarin.
    • You can drop the Lockpick after you are done.
    • Drop all of the loot other than coins.
  • Once finished, Home Teleport.
  • Speak to Duke Horacio in the castle to start Rune Mysteries.
  • Start The Restless Ghost and complete it until you get the skull.
    • Get some Leather Gloves from the spawn by Father Urhney. DO NOT FORGET THIS.
  • Speak to Archmage Sedridor to continue Rune Mysteries.
  • Head to Draynor Village and buy a Chronicle again.
    • It should still have some charges, but buy more if you ever run out.
  • Chronicle Teleport and continue Rune Mysteries by speaking to Aubury.
  • Chronicle Teleport, then walk back to Lumbridge and complete The Restless Ghost.
  • Claim a Training bow and Training arrows from the Ranged combat tutor.
  • Continue and complete Rune Mysteries.
  • Buy wine from Fortunato and head to the H.A.M. Hideout.
  • Steal from H.A.M. Members until you get a Rusty sword and an uncut opal.
    • There is technically a 1/96 chance your rusty sword won't work, so you could get 2.
  • Reclaim your lamp from X Marks the Spot. Save it for now.
  • Head to Port Sarim and purchase some items from Wydin.
    • a few cheese
    • raw beef
    • raw chicken
    • A few other random items for food like cabbage and bananas. Wine lowers you combat stats so you don't want it for this.
  • Safepot and kill a Giant rat nearby with Ranged for the meat.
    • Drop the bow and arrows afterwards.
  • Take the boat to Ardougne.
  • Head north to safe spot and poison a bear for some raw bear meat.
  • Take the boat back to Rimmington.
  • Collect some snape grass west of the Crafting guild for later.
  • Complete Druidic Ritual.
  • Complete Witch's House.
    • Safe spot the boss and kill it with poison.
    • If you don't know how to safe spot the first 2 phases watch the video.
    • Keep the first form in combat with you by occasionally tanking a hit, or it can despawn.
  • (Optional) If you would like, you could accept more risk and start the Wilderness Agility section right now rather than continue to gain more Hitpoints levels.
    • This video talks about some pros and cons of doing this.
    • You will still need to come back and finish the remaining quests from this section later.
    • If you go this route, use the X Marks the Spot lamp on Hitpoints.
      • Also collect your 1k xp lamp from Historian Minas and use it on Hitpoints.
  • Use the X Marks the Spot lamp on Herblore.
    • If you are coming back later after having used this lamp already, you can buy a Greenman's ale to boost to level 10 during the Dig Site.
  • Use the Fishing Trawler minigame teleport.
  • Head south into Yanille and view Aleck's Hunter Emporium for the diary step.
  • Return north and have Tindel Marchant identify your rusty sword for the diary step.
  • Head out on a game of Fishing Trawler for the diary step.
    • You don't need to finish the game.
  • Head into Ardougne and steal a silk. Hold on to it for later.
  • Have Wizard Cromperty teleport you to the Rune essence mine for the diary step.
  • Check what pets you have insured with Probita for the diary step.
  • Use some prayer and restore your prayer points at the Ardougne church for the diary step.
  • Buy a rope from the general store.
  • Head to the Gnome Stronghold and into the Grand Tree.
  • Buy some items from Hudo for Plague City quest.
    • Dwellberries
    • Chocolate dust
    • Bucket of milk
  • Return to Ardougne and complete Plague City.
    • There is a bucket spawn near the start of the quest.
  • Sell your silk to the Silk trader for 60 coins for the diary step.
  • Steal some cakes.
  • Complete Biohazard.
    • You will need to poison the Mourner.
      • Keep him in combat by tanking hits as he can despawn.
    • Don't forget your Fishing Trawler minigame teleport to get back to the area.
  • Enter the Combat Training Camp for the final step of the Ardougne Easy Diary.
    • Do not collect the rewards at this time.
  • Head to Karamja and complete Jungle Potion.
  • Purchase the needed items for The Dig Site in the Karamja General Store. Get the tea during the quest from the tea stall in east Varrock.
  • Complete The Dig Site.
  • Complete Merlin's Crystal.
    • Make sure you still have some combat xp available to kill 2 enemies with poison.
      • If you don't, you can clean more finds to make this up.
    • If you have an alt you can use it to help with Sir Mordred: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DvnhLKAi5xI
  • Claim your xp lamps from Historian Minas and use them on Hitpoints.
  • Clean finds in the Varrock Museum for Antique lamp (Varrock Museum) until you reach 30 Hitpoints so you can use the diary lamps, plus 1 additional lamp.
    • This will be 6 lamps total if I have done my math right and takes about 2 hours depending on RNG and effort.
    • Remember this lamping is optional. If you just don't want to do it, then just skip this and go with fewer HP.
      • If you are on the fence, you can always just try it at lower hp and see how goes, then decide if you want to come back or not.
  • Fishing Trawler minigame teleport and collect your rewards from the Ardougne Easy Diary.
    • Use the lamp on Hitpoints to reach 32 Hitpoints. If you are short a bit, just go back and clean finds for 1 more lamp.
  • Start Dragon Slayer I so you can get an Anti-dragon shield.
  • This is the default tank build setup with 32 Hitpoints, 40 Prayer and 13 combat.
    • The next section will discuss some other optional builds you could go for.
Wilderness Agility

Wilderness Agility

[edit | edit source]

  • (Optional) If this gets too frustrating, then you can always make your gp using another method. Refer to UIM Money Making for ideas on other methods to use.
    • Seriously though, Wilderness Agility is OP. Give it a real try and don't give up if you die once.
    • You still need to get 70+ Agility for later. The Brimhaven course works well for this.
  • Collect gp until you have 160k total at the Agility Pyramid to get started. This should also get you 52 Agility.
    • If you die on your first trip out you will sadly have to come back here for more gp.
    • If you ever get frustrated at the Wildy Couse, remember this grind and how much slower gp your alternatives are. Agility Pyramid (with some more Agility levels) is about the same gp/h as Thieving.
  • Train at the Wilderness Agility Course until you have 70+ Agility and at least 10m gp.
    • YOU NEED TO WATCH THE VIDEO ON HOW TO TANK AT THE COURSE.
      • Yes it is long, but I spent the time to make it to keep your ass alive!
        • Ok, for real. At least watch the first part where I show you the skeleton mechanics even if you skip the rest.
    • Use the setup shown in the example below.
      • See This Video for how to re-gear when you die.
      • Buy the Cooked karambwans at The Shrimp and Parrot for your first trip out.
      • You will get a looting bag automatically when you pay the 150k fee.
      • Use blighted supplies on later trips once you get them.
    • Sell your loot to Martin Thwait's Lost and Found after each trip.
      • Destroy your looting bag IN THE WILDERNESS to get the loot out and pick it up. Note that other players can see this loot instantly!
      • Store your extra coins in the coffers at Last Man Standing as you go.
      • Sell at least 2-3 per world. Not 1, as it takes too long to be worth it.
    • For your first time out, do about 50 laps and then leave. On later trips, do 100-150+ laps depending on your risk tolerance, build, PKer activity, and tanking skills.
    • If you are interested in making this grind safer/more consistent check out the sections below for some build options and about mass worlds.
    • 10m is just the minimum needed to safely finish the guide, but I highly recommend going for at least 15-20m.
    • There is no way to avoid bringing the blighted supplies with you, so you just have to risk them. After you are done here the guide will have you turn them into Bounty supply crates and sell them for a bit of bonus gp.
      • Do not worry about dying and losing the supplies. It really isn't a huge deal and you can't make the crates without a combat level of 32 to get into Bounty Hunter.
Other Grind Options

This section will go over a few options for skilling grinds you can get a head-start on if you want a break from Agility or while waiting for masses.

  • Work towards one of the other build options.
    • Remember simply cleaning finds for more lamps is always a chill option as well.
  • Fishing to level 53+.
  • Wintertodt to level 99.
    • Do Daddy's Home and Tower of Life to get a few Construction levels first.
    • Make some headless arrows for a few starting Fletching levels. Going to level 20 is fine.
    • Do Forestry as you get the 50 Firemaking to work towards a log basket.
      • You can save your bark in the Forestry kit by death piling and letting the kit de-spawn if you don't have a Magic wardrobe.
  • Vale Totems for the Fletching knife.
    • Make sure to have a Magic wardrobe first. Doing solo Wintertodt can help get this.
  • Cooking to level 70.
  • Mining to level 52.
  • Giant's Foundry for the Smith's outfit.
    • Just use the bucket of water rather than ice gloves.


Mass Worlds

One very powerful way to reduce your risk at the course is by running during mass events hosted by various clans.

During these events, a large number of clan members go to the course together and protect each-other against other PKers.

I have had success with Agility FC and have generally heard good things about them, but you can run with whomever you like.

YOU ARE NOT COMPLETELY SAFE DOING THIS. Don't be fooled, people still die during the masses.

Your biggest threat are dark bow pures that try to pick off low-level accounts in 1-2 special attacks and then escape.

You can mitigate your risk against these by turning on Protect from Ranged.

One strategy is to bring an inventory of blighted super restores with you and camp protect range during the later half of your trip where you are risking more. Then leave once your prayer runs out.

If you are able to 1 tick flick your prayer, you can last a lot longer for more effort.

Don't bank your loot on the mass world as you might get picked off away from everyone else and you have to destroy the looting bag so everyone could see your loot.

  • Read the rules and abide by any instructions for the clan you are going with.
    • If you are running with Agility FC, you must wear a ranged weapon so swap your training sword to a crossbow and bring something else for the webs.
      • You don't need bolts as you won't attack anyone or it would ruin your build. Just look scary...
  • It is viable to only do Agility during the masses and work on other skilling grinds in the meantime.
    • This is a (relatively) safe option but you have to pay attention to when masses are running.
36 Hitpoints Build

If you are interested in going for a bit more protection, but don't want to get too side-tracked, then pushing for a 36 Hitpoint build with some more easy diary lamps can help a lot.

Going from 32 to 36 is a very nice boost for only 1 combat level, and doing these diaries is good for your account in general later.

You should hopefully have enough extra combat xp to do this with your poison dagger, but if not you might need to clean finds instead to make up one of the lamps.

NOTE: This isn't worth the time unless you want to stay at the course a long time. Do not do this if you just want to get your 10-15m and go.

  • Read the next section first and decide if you want to go for Watchtower with your limited remaining combat xp before spending it here.
  • Complete the easy Varrock Diary.
    • Remember you can get bones from the boneyard if needed.
    • Complete Enter the abyss, then craft 1 inventory of runes at the Ourania Altar.
    • Consider getting 41/52 Mining now to use the Rune pickaxe.
    • Complete Temple of the eye.
      • Bring some pure essence with you and leave the Abyss through the Earth portal to craft the runes.
      • Play some Guardians of the rift and loot after each round until you have enough Abyssal pearls for a Mind talisman.
        • You can use the Varrock armour 1.
  • Complete the easy Falador Diary.
    • Complete Daddy's home and Tower of life then use the planks on a few Mahogany homes contracts for the Construction level.
    • Use some of your Magic or Ranged xp on the duck.
  • Complete the easy Lumbridge & Draynor Diary.
    • You will need 2 poisons to complete this.
    • After you are done, you can add the Explorer's ring 1 to your setup for an extra Prayer bonus.
    • To kill the cave bug you have to do a bit extra because of their very high HP regen.
      • Bring your dagger and ranged/magic.
      • Poison the bug as normal.
      • After it gets hit by a 4, attack with with Ranged or Magic to get an extra hit of damage in.
  • If you still have combat xp for the Jogre (it takes 2 poisons), complete the easy Karamja Diary. This should get you 36 Hitpoints.
    • If you are out of xp, just clean finds for a few lamps and call it a day. This diary only gives 1k xp.
Tankman Skiller Build

If you are interested in staying at the wilderness course for a long time to make those mega millions, then you might want to get even more Hitpoints.

Going for 40+ Hitpoints really makes things a lot more comfortable. You can of course get this by cleaning more finds at the museum for awhile longer.

However, if you are interested in exploring more of the skiller lifestyle then you could go for Dynamite(p) and complete more quests without gaining combat xp.

The most direct way to do this is to partially complete Watchtower until you can get the Skavid map and pick up Cave nightshade.

Honestly going this far off the rails definitely isn't going to save more time than it takes to do, but if you are enjoying exploring this playstyle then give it a shot!

  • It isn't the end of the world if you have to gain an extra Attack or Defense level, but if you are out of combat xp you can try to go for growing nightshade instead.
    • There are also lots of methods involving alts that you could look into.
  • Partially complete Tai Bwo Wannai Trio until you can use the kp poison on an iron spear.
    • There is a reasonably good chance you will have to get the 65 Fishing requirement as you can burn the 1 Karambwan you get.
  • Use the kp spear to kill a Green dragon in the far east wilderness for the Dragon bones.
  • Partially complete Watchtower until you get the Skavid map.
    • There is another npc to poison in the quest.
  • Get the Firemaking level for the dynamite and look up guides on how to do quests as a skiller.
  • Complete quests like One Small Favor, A Tail of Two Cats or more diaries for extra Hitpoints.
MTA and Protect Melee

MTA and Protect Melee

[edit | edit source]
  • This money, plus gp from other methods you will do later, should be enough to last the whole guide. However, if you find yourself running short then check out UIM Money Making for some ideas.
  • Keep all of your blighted supplies in your inventory for now. They will be turned into Bounty Hunter Crates later.
  • Head to the Grand Exchange.
  • Put up a purchase order for a bond for 2m, then cancel the offer. Leave the money there.
  • Go to the Ferox Enclave. Don't use your minigame teleport.
  • Put all of your remaining money in the coffer there.
  • Unnote some food in case you are attacked on the way to mage bank.
  • Grab an iron dagger from the spawn north of the enclave in the graveyard.
  • Go to the Mage Arena bank.
    • Use the wilderness lever to get there faster.
  • Collect your money from the bond at the banker.
  • Buy the listed runes.
    • 500 Mind runes
    • 2000 Nature runes
    • 1000 Cosmic runes
    • 800 Law runes
    • 1000 Water runes
    • 1000 Earth runes
  • (Optional but Recommended) Buy extra runes for the Master wand. It is very strong after the buff and getting the points now is great Magic xp.
    • 1000 Law
    • 2200 Nature
    • 1000 Cosmic
  • Return to Ferox Enclave with your minigame teleport and put all but 4000 coins into the coffer.
  • Chronicle teleport or home teleport and walk/canoe to Varrock.
  • Head to Varrock and buy a staff of air and a staff of fire.
  • Head to the Edgeville Dungeon and kill Thugs for 15 Magic and a Looting bag.
    • Use Wind Strike with the staff of air equipped.
    • Put your blighted supplies in the Looting bag once you get it.
  • Drop the mind runes after.
  • Head to Mage Training Arena and get enough points to obtain Bones to Peaches, a Rune Pouch, Master wand, and a Mud Rune.
    • DO NOT BUY THE RUNE POUCH, Master wand, OR Mud Rune YET! That will come later!
    • Creature Graveyard: 351 points (831 with Master Wand).
      • You can drop the earth and water runes after you are done and rebuy more later.
      • The other reward runes are not super important. You can drop them or save them to sell/alch/use later.
      • Just get enough for Bones to peaches first and then come back to this room after you unlock that.
    • Telekinetic Theatre: 351 points (831 with Master Wand).
      • Keep the air staff, or drop it for space and buy another later.
      • You should have some extra law runes leftover, save them for teleports.
    • Enchanting Chamber with Lvl-3 Enchant until you have used all of your cosmic runes. You need at least 3515 points at the end (8315 with Master wand).
    • Alchemist's Playground until you reach 501 points (1031 with Master wand).
      • Use up any remaining nature runes as well for extra xp.
      • You can deliver coins in large stacks now if you would like. There isn't a maximum anymore.
  • Buy Bones to Peaches.
  • NOTE: Do not actually buy the Master wand for a long time. Let it wait until you are farther in your account and ready for things like bursting Slayer that use it.
  • Keep the staff of air.
  • Drop the staff of fire.
  • Minigame teleport to Clan Wars to get your cash stack back out.
  • Head to Varrock and buy some runes:
    • 500 Fire Runes
    • 500 Earth Runes
    • 500 Water Runes
    • 20 Air runes (For Waterfall)
    • 500 Death Runes for Wind blast (If you run out just buy more).
  • Do Daddy's Home.
    • Pick up logs in the Lumberyard to make the planks.
    • Complete 2 beginner Mahogany Homes contracts with the supplies.
    • Remember you now have a house to teleport to.
  • Re-obtain your Ardougne cloak 1 for the teleport.
    • Don't forget it is relatively close to a Spirit Tree.
  • Get a Banana hat to improve your fashion.
  • Go pick up some Boots of lightness from the Temple of Ikov (dungeon).
    • You will need a light source and a knife/slash weapon.
  • For the next sections, you can get some cakes in Ardougne for food.
    • You can also buy rope and iron axe in the general store for the quests.
  • Head to Barbarian Assault and skip the tutorial to unlock the minigame teleport.
  • While there, start Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl.
    • The guide will take you near several of the bars in the next few steps, you can complete them as you go if you would like.
  • Complete Waterfall Quest until you go to maze and get the pebble.
    • Just partially complete it for now, you will need to clear up your bagged items before going in the tomb.
  • Complete Tree Gnome Village and Fight Arena while in the area.
  • Head to any spot where you can go into the Wilderness and destroy your Looting Bag to get your blighted supplies back out.
    • YOU MUST BE STANDING IN THE WILDERNESS OR THE ITEMS WILL BE LOST.
    • Obviously be safe and don't do this if anyone is nearby.
  • Head to Bounty Hunter and create as many Bounty supply crates as you can.
  • Head to the Rogues Den and sell the crates.

The Fragment of Seren

At the end of the quest, you will be tasked with facing the Fragment of Seren bossfight. This fight is not extremely hard, if you are well prepared.

The best way to complete the fight is to utilize Phoenix necklaces, triggered by eating Nightshade to nullify the damage of her big attack.

This works because Phoenix necklaces have a special property of clearing out attacks pending on the player, which includes her big attack.

However many other types of self-damage such as the Dwarven Rock Cake are disabled during the special attack, so don't try to use them.

Setup:

The recommended setup for the fight is shown below. This will utilize Iban Blast with the Mystic robes set for damage, and a shortbow of any kind.

A shortbow is used for a bit of extra range over something like knives. You can hunt some chincompas if you would like, but it is not needed.

You may also choose to use the Void Knight magic armor instead of mystic, they are very similar damage output.

The videos provide more details on the setup and how to gear up, and there are plenty of tutorials online if you need more help.

If you do not have enough Diamonds, then the most direct way to get them is to obtain a Fire cape and purchase them in Mor Ul Rek.

If you die in the fight, remember that this is a Death Bank NOT a Death Pile. If you die again before reclaiming, such as resetting other death piles, your items will be lost!

Epilogue and PvM Guide

Epilogue and PvM Guide

[edit | edit source]

Once you have finished up Song of the Elves, the path from here on out is yours to create!

By now you should be comfortable enough with the Ultimate Ironman game mode to handle things like questing on your own.

However, this section will provide you a bit of guidance and suggestions as to what you might want to do next!

Lumbridge Elite Diary

From an efficiency point of view, your next major goal should be to work towards finishing the Elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary. With the most notable requirement being the Quest point cape.

Not only is questing a very good way to advance your account in general, but this diary is particularly important for Ultimate Ironmen because of the ability to use Fairy rings without a Dramen staff.

This perk is very nice to have as it saves the hassle of periodically obtaining a Dramen staff or purchasing a Lunar staff from Perdu, and saves an inventory slot for a lot of activities.

The extra block slots from the diary and quest points are very helpful for Slayer, and the alchemy effect is very handy for alching things while on another spellbook.

Overall, all of these benefits, combined with the general benefits of questing, makes going for this diary a very worthwhile endevour.

Skilling

Another way to progress your account would be by settling in to some of the longer skilling grinds to get a lot of useful upgrades and unlocks.

The downside to this is that skilling to high levels takes a very long time, and if you were truly being efficient there are hundreds of hours of skilling to do before you even touch PvM.

The list below provides examples of just some of the many useful unlocks you can get through skilling.
  • Ability to craft Wrath runes.
  • Build an Ornate rejuvenation pool.
  • Agility level for various high-level shortcuts.
  • Ability to make super combat potions.
  • Ability to steal from master farmers without failing.
  • Crafting requirements for powerful jewelry.
  • Ability to fletch Amethyst darts.
  • Lots of loot from Hunter rumours, and/or fast Ranged training with chinchompas.
  • Mining level for Amethyst.
  • Smithing level for diaries and to craft the crystal equipment.
  • Ability to fish Minnows for noted Sharks.
  • Ability to cook noted sharks.
  • Lots of loot and xp from Wintertodt.
  • Diary unlocks from higher Woodcutting.
  • Farm higher level seeds and extra spirit trees.
  • There are plenty more. Skills are important!
Slayer and PvM

Finally, the thing that most people are probably eager to do is jump into bossing, combat and other PvM activities.

However, as an Ultimate Ironman killing bosses and obtaining gear is actually a bit tricky because each item you obtain takes up your limited bag space.

This means that you need to be mindful of what items you plan to get, their order, and what items you can simply skip entirely.

In order to assist you with your planning, a separate page has been created that outlines a core gear upgrade path to smoothly progress your account.

You do not have to follow this path exactly of course, but you can use it as a reference to help you decide what you want to do.
